utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: While the Judges -- while the witness is coming in, I'll deal with three administrative matters. There are -- there is a third motion to add exhibits by General Ojdanic. There is no objection from the Prosecution to this, and therefore that application is granted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's then a fourth one and, Mr. Stamp, are you aware of this fourth application because, if possible, we would like to deal with it quite quick --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It can be dealt with quite quickly, perhaps tomorrow if we could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If you could look at it and tell us what your position is or even e-mail a position, that can be dealt with. And lastly, there is an application on behalf of Mr. Sainovic to specify accurately in a substitute sheet the sections of a video which were played. I doubt if there can possibly be any argument that that's the appropriate course to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: On the basis of what is being represented here, I doubt it myself, but I would prefer to deal with it formally and respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, if you could look at that also and if you can indicate the position tomorrow, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That will be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will continue in a moment with cross-examination by Mr. Ivetic, where we left off yesterday. Please again bear in mind that the solemn declaration you made at the beginning continues to apply to your evidence today. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, General Gajic. I would like to take up where we left off yesterday and the area I was about to go into. I'd like to focus your attention on the briefing of the staff of the high command memorialized in Exhibit 3D721, and that would be page 2 of the English and page 2 of the B/C/S or Serbian as well. And, General, I'm going to go ahead and ask you the question and you can, if need be, review the documents once they come up on the screen. During this briefing which is on the 3rd of April, 1999, you are recorded as saying that your service had information about paramilitaries, saying volunteers had come to Kosovo as members of the reserve force of the MUP, and that 32 such volunteers had been sent back from Kosovo for crimes. Now, what precise paramilitary or volunteer formations are you talking about at this briefing on the 3rd of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The reserve MUP was not referred to. This has to do with volunteers from the 175th Infantry Brigade. Among them was a group of volunteers from -- headed by Vlado Zmajevic, who had committed a crime in the village of Zegra in the municipality of Gnjilane where eight civilians were killed. There was looting as well. These civilians were robbed, their money, jewellery, et cetera was taken. As far as I can remember they even torched their houses. This group was identified, arrested, a criminal report was filed, they were all convicted. Vlado Zmajevic was sentenced to 20 years in prison and the rest got one-year prison sentences and more than that. There was a total of seven individuals involved. Then the commander of the army, General Pavkovic, since there were 25 other volunteers there too, so it's a total of 32, they behaved in contravention of military regulations and international regulations. They were returned from the unit. They were returned to the centre in the village of Medja near Nis, and they were sent away. Another measure was taken --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please wait for the interpretation to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- If you like we can discuss in detail later and I have some questions on that. What I'm focusing on so there's no mistake in the translation I'll read the section to you. The part of your briefing that begins, the second page on page 2 of the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It is too fast and we don't have the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the interpreters say you are reading too quickly and they don't have the text to follow. Could you start again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, I'll start again. [Interpretation] "There are problems concerning the territory with paramilitary formations. There are problems -- there is information that there are volunteers who had come to Kosovo and Metohija without the army being aware of it, and that is the MUP reserve forces."

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had information to that effect. Now I cannot remember specifically what this was about, but we did have this intelligence about it. And certainly that would not have been said had we not had that kind of information, and there is also -- I do apologise. There is a proposal here to make the MUP aware of this, and I think that we did inform the MUP about this but that we did not give an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you're continuing too quickly. You must allow us -- even where you're speaking different languages -- well it should normally happen but you seem to be jumping in with your question before the answer is translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I'm not listening to the English translation. Maybe that would help.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, General, given the date of this briefing as being the 3rd of April, 1999, and given that of the matters you have testified about that your service had knowledge of, the Skorpions in Podujevo, that event that occurred at the end of March, could be the only paramilitary group that your service had knowledge of based upon your testimony these past several days. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not quite, not fully correct. You are right on one thing concerning the Skorpions paramilitary group, but we also had information that proved to be correct later in relation to one of Arkan's groups. At the meeting held on the 17th of May at the office of President -- then-President Milosevic, which was confirmed to us by Rade Markovic, head of the state security sector, he confirmed both. And thirdly, we had information about a group, a paramilitary group, that had come from Republika Srpska whose head was Nedeljko Karasek, nicknamed Legenda, who before the war was head of the special anti-terrorist units of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We'll get to all that later, sir, but this is April we are talking about. You did not find out about the Arkan units until your meeting May the 17th, is that correct, or should I say is General Vasiljevic correct when he testified to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm not sure if General Vasiljevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll strike that part of the -- I'll strike that part of the question I think it is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that you only found out about the Arkan members of the JSO during the meeting with President Milosevic on the 17th of May, 1999, some two months after this briefing took place?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, earlier on we had information about Arkan, but it was hard to check it; however, we did have information that he was down there in Kosovo -- in actual fact, in Kosovo Polje, where there was a training centre. That is what our knowledge was. Then on the 17th of May we said that and, as I've already said, Rade Markovic claimed to us that that was correct, and he explained how all of this went. But we'll probably get to that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, we'll deal with the May 17th meeting later, but let's talk again about April. What were your sources for this information about paramilitaries in the reserve force of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these were operative sources. Among them were some persons from these same paramilitary units, because these are paramilitary units that appeared in 1991 and they went through Croatian and Bosnian theatres of war. So we intensively followed their activity because very often they even acted vis-a-vis the army. They tried to recruit some soldiers and even officers to join them. We had to follow that in order to prevent that, because then and particularly later we had a precise position; namely, not to allow the establishment of paramilitary formations in the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So you're saying that this information did not come from your security organs in the field, but rather from contacts that your service had with paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means from the security organs who had contacts with individuals who were members of these paramilitary formations; that is to say, security organs -- I mean, they were their operative sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Which particular security organs? Where were they located? Were these just general rumours or were there specific facts from specific persons in specific locations?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specific facts from specific individuals in specific locations. I will just tell you as far as the paramilitary unit of Slobodan Medic, Boca, is concerned, since most of the people had been recruited from the territory of Vojvodina, then that was under the jurisdiction of the 12th counter-intelligence group, and they covered the territory of Vojvodina and they had very good positions there, very good contacts. They sent reports and even they had some recorded conversations, intercepts; that is to say that there is reliable information and information that had been checked out.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you help me out, how many kilometres are there between Vojvodina and Kosovo? And are you telling me that the security organ in Vojvodina followed the happenings of this group in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand it or I wasn't specific enough. The security organs, the ones that I referred to in the territory of Vojvodina, they followed their activity in collecting, organising, and sending persons to Kosovo. And the counter-intelligence organs in Kosovo had the task of registering their presence in the territory of Kosovo and trying to see what it was that they were doing there. It was a bit difficult to establish that, but that is what their task was. So there was this coordination from the beginning to the end, if I can put it that way, to try to gain full insight into their presence and their activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you already knew about these Skorpions in Podujevo as of the 3rd of April, then why is it, sir, that it took until May the 13th for your service to prepare 3D1059, the information report giving info about a crime that occurred on the 31st of March and that the Skorpion -- the so-called Skorpions, actually the reservist SAJ were ordered out of Kosovo according to that information by the commander of the 334th Brigade of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where you got this information, the 4th of April. They were first there in March, and on the 31st of March they committed this crime in Podujevo when they killed ten children and two adults. That is when they were removed to Prolom Banja. We had some information, and I also had the briefing at the staff of the security -- of the General Staff, but we in addition to that informed the State Security Service. Very often this was in the following form. The chief of the security administration called the persons in charge in the security administration and asked what this was all about; however, we never received an answer --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness because there is background noise from the other microphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Because I will have very interesting testimony from General Vasiljevic to present to you. Now, with respect to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you're not seeking an answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah, we could spend some time on it now. I was trying to move along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But let's bring up 3D1059.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for that I will repeat the question. General, if as you have said the briefing from the 3rd of April before the high command, the chief of the high command, dealt in part with the Skorpions, that is to say that you had operative information about the Skorpions, these reservist SAJ members that were former Skorpions, as of that date why did it take so long for your service to prepare this exhibit, this information sheet on May the 13th?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's not the one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is to say that we provided information in succession of this problem and that we had information about Slobodan Medic, Boca; however, it was hard to check that. Maybe I'll be a bit cynical when I said that Slobodan Medic, Boca, never reported to the service that he was going to Kosovo, so this was strictly confidential, secret. They did not go down there to wage war; they went down there to loot. Because the information of Slobodan Medic, Boca, dated back to 1991 --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... If you do we're going to lose sight of what we're looking for and I appreciate maybe that you would like to perhaps obscure things, but I would like to get to the truth of matters. Now, let's focus on this particular -- it's actually 3D1055, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise to you. I have to say something to you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... In 1992, in the -- during the time-period of the conflict elsewhere, the Skorpions were under the command of VJ General Loncar; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Skorpions were disbanded in 1996 before the Kosovo conflict even began?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what that means, disbanded. They were so mobile that -- and they were so well-connected, that at every moment they could rally together quickly. Perhaps they were formally disbanded.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe -- you said you were following them, were they disbanded in 1996 or not if you were following them so intensively as you state?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You keep insisting. Let me answer. Formally, they were disbanded, but they were always prepared at any point in time to rally together and to be engaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, again, if you knew about the Skorpions and the incident on the 31st of May -- excuse me, 31st of March, and were referring about it in April, what was the reason to write the document which is now up on the screen, 3D1055, all the way in May, May 13th of 1999, essentially recycling the same information that you had in the beginning of April?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we wanted to be 100 per cent sure about what we were reporting the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command about; and from what I know this information was also sent to the then-President Slobodan Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, that wasn't that hard. Now we can move to another aspect of this group, these reservist SAJ, we had a former Skorpion member and a SAJ reservist testify here under oath for the Prosecution, it was Mr. Stoparic, he was an eye-witness to the Podujevo incident and he states at transcript 748 lines 15 to 21 that the SAJ senior officers tried to render assistance to the wounded Albanians and that then the SAJ commander Tutinac himself angrily ordered them a back to Serbia this was at transcript page 749 line 3 to 750, line 17, this all occurred on the 31st of March. Did your information from your operative sources or security organs include these facts about the actions of the MUP superior officers in condemning the killings and disciplining those involved?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, it's just that I believe that it's not Mr. Tutinac. His name is different. I think that it was General Trajkovic in person who commanded the special anti-terrorist units at the time, and it is correct that after the event he intervened urgently and sent them to Prolom Banja.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, if I can -- first of all, I'm telling you what Mr. Stoparic testified to. If you think that you know better than he what he eye-witnessed, that's a different story. If I refresh your recollection, wasn't Trajkovic wounded several days before this and therefore not in the field, but recovering, I believe, in the hospital with a wound where the persons with him had been killed?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic is kindly asked to slow down when asking questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... Is not the main thing whether it is this person or that person. I agree that measures were taken immediately from a high position from SAJ for them to return to Prolom Banja, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, the particular facts and details are important to us, especially what your service knew and what it reported when it makes such grandiose claims of problems of paramilitaries. Because from the testimony Here you're talking about two incidents both of which were processed by the authorities and that's why it's important. Now, let me ask you this Mr. Stoparic went on at page 771, line 21 through 22, in particular, but throughout his testimony, to explicitly state: "I was a SAJ reservist with regular documents about my status." And this was something he said he was proud of. Now, am I correct that the information from your sources indeed verifies Mr. Stoparic's testimony that these former Skorpion members who were in the SAJ reserve were all SAJ reservists with documentation?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Arkan and all of his people also had MUP IDs and IDs of the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Did Arkan and his men have MUP IDs?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know for a fact that in 1994 and 1995 this was true; as for later, I don't know, but I assume that they did have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Speculating I should say ...

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] No comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Am I correct that the information that your service had is that Arkan's men never had documentation from the RJB, the "Resor Javne Bezbednosti"?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that. It was happening in 1998 and 1999 if they had documents, but I do know -- please, I do know that on the 17th of May, Rade Markovic confirmed everything that we had and presented at a meeting on the 17th of May in front of President Milosevic and the generals --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... We'll get to that May 17th meeting. I asked you a specific question about the SAJ reservists that were formerly Skorpions. Rather than answer my question, you chose to move on to Arkan. Now, I'm more than happy to explore Arkan because I have some material here about that, but I would ask that you please answer my questions and we'll go through this a lot quicker and a lot easier. Now, just to finish up with this Arkan issue that you have opened up, I'm going to ask you -- you say you don't know about 1998, et cetera, we know that. We know that your knowledge only covers 1994 and 1995. You've already answered that. During 1994 and 1995, isn't it a fact that Arkan's men never had documentation from the RJB "Resor Javne Bezbednosti", yes or no?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, you said you knew about them having IDs in 1994 and 1995, so I'm limiting my question to those two years, General.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that they did have documentation from the RDB or not, is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did have it. We even had examples. We had those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The counsel needs to wait until the end of the translation. Perhaps he can put his headphones on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you'll need to put on your headphones and listen to the translation because I haven't alerted you as often as the interpreter has mentioned the issue of speed. So please allow the gap before asking the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, I think I have to clarify something. It looks like the transcript -- at least the interpretation of my -- of my Serbian as RDB, I actually asked about the RJB, so perhaps I have to ask that question of the witness again to make sure we're on the same page because he might have answered the way I expected him to answer instead of the way I thought he'd answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is it your information that the Arkanovci had documentation only from the RDB in 1994 and 1995, not the RJB?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was connected to the MUP. It was just that the RDB is the other MUP line. There is the RJB and there is the RDB, but their IDs were from the RDB, you are right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, then it was a translation error, I think, although I was listening to the Serbian and still thought it was different but we'll see. Now, if we can get back to my question - and I'll beg you to answer it - all of these former Skorpions in Podujevo of whom you had information were all legitimate, documented reservist SAJ police; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, then, let me -- hold on one second then. I think we'll move on to another exhibit. First of all, sir, let me ask you, given your definition of paramilitaries that you used the other day, yesterday I think it was, on questioning from Judge Bonomy, if someone in uniform is formally and legally a member of the MUP, then they cannot be called a paramilitary, isn't that correct, since the MUP is a legitimate state organ?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you say that you don't have any information that these persons in Podujevo, these Medic people, Boca people, were reservist members of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would ask for Exhibit 6D988 to be brought up and in advance I'll bring to everyone's attention that this is a document that we recently uploaded and do not have English translation for, so I'll have to have either myself or the witness read relevant portions of it and we'll submit it for identification purposes upon receival of an official translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, since we don't have an English translation of this document, could you please identify this document and tell us if, in fact, you ever saw it before taking into account at the bottom of the document it says: [Interpretation] "For Colonel Gajic."

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. And is this a report from your security organ within the 3rd Army command dated the 16th of May, 1999?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the security section of the 3rd Army command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And could you please, sir, so that I don't make any mistakes, read for us the two middle paragraphs that deal with these individuals led by Boca Medic, the information that you had in May of 1999.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The part that begins: "Colonel Sredojevic" or the part that begins: "We are also in possession." In paragraph 2 it says: "Colonel Sredojevic, who is mentioned by the security department of the Prokuplje Platoon had telephone contact with Vucicevic who is chief of the Prokuplje MUP, who through his superior intervened and said that everything is legal and that there would be no problems. We also have checked information that Major-General Djakovic Milan an operative in the 3rd Army command recognised in the said group a certain Slobodan Medic, a.k.a. Boca," it says here Goca but it's Boca, "who he asked what his task was that he came for, to which the said person replied that he had come on the order of the MUP General Rodja." And then it goes on to say: "We are continuing with further checking and gathering of information."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Does that refresh your recollection as to whether you had operative information that, in fact, these individuals under Boca Medic were, in fact, reservists within SAJ?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. No sense in beating a dead horse. Let me ask you this: General Rodja from the MUP that is mentioned, do you at least have knowledge of who that individual is, what the nickname -- what the full name of that individual is; and is that the RJB chief and deputy minister of interior General Vlastimir Djordjevic as the man who was ordering the deployment of these SAJ reservists?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is Vlastimir Djordjevic called Rodja. He is one of the assistant ministers of the MUP and he was the chief of the public security section.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, based on your intensive following of the happenings and occurrences dealing with this group and based upon your many organs in the field, do you have knowledge that, in fact, the SAJ reservists, the former Skorpions who actually perpetrated the shooting in Podujevo, not only were disciplined by the MUP, were taken out of Kosovo and not returned, criminal denunciations were filed, and these individuals eventually received the maximum sentences for their crimes in the Serbian courts. Do you have that knowledge or information, sir?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have information that after Podujevo they were returned to Prolom Banja, and then after that they came back. This information is actually based on data, and I have to say this again. Rade Markovic said on the 17th of May at a meeting with Milosevic, it's something he said there, that's the first thing. The second thing is before judiciary organs certain measures were taken, and from what I recall there was a trial in Nis, and one of those members of this formation who apparently carried out this crime, his name is Sasa Cvijin or something like that, he was sentenced to 20 years' imprisonment, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. One more question on this topic before we move back to my original order of questions. During the testimony of General Vasiljevic at transcript page 9005 lines 6 through 12, General Vasiljevic confirmed that apart from this one incident in Podujevo at the end of March 1999, your service had no evidence whatsoever of any further crimes committed by this group of SAJ reservists when they were redeployed to Kosovo. I take it that that is your position as well?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All we had was information that they were returned to Kosovo again, and that sometime between the 10th and the 12th of May they were definitely returned or brought back from Kosovo, that they no longer appeared in Kosovo territory. We had no information for that second time that they were there, about them having committed any crimes -- or actually, I apologise, it was some kind of information but I don't recall it exactly. I think that in the testimony of General Vasiljevic here he mentioned that. I was following that, but I don't remember. I think it was something that happened in Gnjilane, I don't remember whether it was correct or not. But in any case, when they were returned sometime between the 10th and the 15th of May, they were no longer brought back to Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, that's a very interesting answer. Did you read the witness statement of General Vasiljevic where he mentioned Gnjilane and tried to tie it to the SAJ reservists? Did you have access to General Vasiljevic's statement?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have the statement. I don't recall that, but if this was something that General Vasiljevic stated, then knowing him that he wouldn't say anything without having the facts at hand, that's probably what it was. It's not something that was going through my head. I mean, it's possible. You cannot remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, it would be interesting since the Vasiljevic statement was only given to us a few days before General Vasiljevic testified, but let me ask you this because in his statement Vasiljevic does mention Gnjilane and does try to tie that to the SAJ reservists. But in his sworn testimony in re-direct upon questioning of the Prosecution, he confirmed that, in fact, his statement in the written statement was inaccurate, that the event in Gnjilane was, in fact, this Zegra group that you mentioned earlier, which he said, and I quote at transcript page 9107 lines 5 to 17: "The perpetrators in Zegra were a paramilitary group that belonged to the army, a group of volunteers I think it was." Does that refresh your recollection as to whether your service had --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, paramilitary group.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm only repeating for you your friend General Vasiljevic's words; please don't take it out on me. If he's wrong, then say he's wrong --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Does that refresh your recollection that your service's information was that the event -- the incident in Gnjilane was not tied to the SAJ reservists?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I answered that question. I don't recall that, but it is correct what I said earlier about Zegra and Gnjilane and who committed the crime there. So if I were to assert -- I mean, I don't have facts, I don't have proof, so I do not wish to say anything that I could not stand behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'd like to move on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, two matters. It's not clear -- it may be clear to you, Mr. Ivetic. It's not clear to me what the witness is saying about who is responsible for Gnjilane. What's your understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, let me ask the witness, Your Honour, because I think that's the most important thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The crime in Gnjilane was this crime in the village of Zegra; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question was -- your question was when 32 volunteers were shown here, I said what it was all about. So there is a group of volunteers there from the 185th Brigade in the Zegra village, this is in Gnjilane, and they killed seven civilians, and that's how it happened. But they were all identified and arrested, and the chief of that group Vlado Zmajevic who was originally from Niksic was sentenced to 20 years' imprisonment, while the others were sentenced to sentences ranging from one to several years' of imprisonment. This is something I know for sure, these facts are correct. As for the other things that you asked me about, I really am unable to say anything. I cannot say anything that I am not sure about that is not completely clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, you earlier said that they were from the 175th Infantry Brigade. You now say the 185th. Can you clarify that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's possible that I was mistaken, but what I meant to say was the 175th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On the incident in Podujevo, do I gather properly from your evidence that only one person was convicted by the court in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you did understand that correctly, one person was sentenced, but that trial is still not completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that group were thereafter, after the incident, had led to their being sent out of Kosovo, they were then redeployed back into Kosovo in the month of May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Sometime between the 10th and the 15th, they were brought back to Belgrade and they did not appear there anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Under whose authority did they return to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I can say is that what was said by Rade Markovic on the 17th of May at the meeting with the president, I can say that, too, that's the only thing I can say. He said that they returned to Kosovo and that Rodja and Obrad did not respect the agreement. He said that literally. I understood that to mean that the agreement was for them not to go there anymore and for them to be banned access there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And when you say "he said," are you referring to Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Markovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Markovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The chief of the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you say his words were that Rodja, who is Djordjevic, and Obrad, who no doubt is Stevanovic, did not observe the agreement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and the agreement was that Medic and the Skorpions no longer be allowed to go to Kosovo. These were the words of Rade Markovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to move to the trip that you testified that General Geza Farkas took in -- into Kosovo. Now, you have -- when I asked you about your briefings and what paramilitaries you were talking about, you've been rather explicit that you're talking about the Medic group, the Arkan's people that you say were in -- that Rade Markovic said were in the JSO, and these Vukovi from the Drina and these perhaps Pauk, but those are the only things you've testified about. What were the reasons that General Geza Farkas went to Kosovo because it surely couldn't be the MUP since you didn't have jurisdiction over the MUP. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I explained that on Friday when I testified, but I can repeat that. He did not go for the MUP, that's true. He went --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's good enough for me, sir.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now -- because it goes into my next question. Now, when you said General Farkas returned and commented to you over the telephone, I believe, There are a lot of problems, and he mentioned paramilitaries, robbery, crimes, rapes, and looting. Could you please tell us precisely which paramilitaries Farkas identified to you as the basis of his observations?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a telephone conversation. I had the regular briefing. I knew that he was coming back, and I wanted to have some initial information because he was, or rather, General Ojdanic was always pressuring me - if I can use that expression - with regard to that. So he told me what he could over the telephone; he did not say anything specific. I authentically conveyed what was said to me. Of course over the telephone he did not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, you -- well, you did have occasion to meet with him afterwards. Did he elaborate at that point in time what paramilitaries he was talking about when he said there were many problems or a lot of problems with paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Farkas, when he returned on the morning of the 7th of May, we had a collegium of the chief of administration, and he presented his impressions as to what he noticed during that brief period of time down there. Because he had other questions to deal with as well. In addition to having commended the work of the security organs, without going specifically into any one of the problems or any one of the cases concerned, without mentioning any specific paramilitary formation, because that was not his focus. He just informed us about this; that is to say, he did not specifically refer to this or that paramilitary formation and he even did not even go into specific crimes. It was later that we worked on that. I spoke about that already, but there will probably be other references to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So is it your testimony, sir, that when the head of your service, a service which is intensively following events on the ground, especially related to crimes, when your head of service says, There are a lot of problems with paramilitaries, no one bothers to go into details and no details are actually in possession of your service, is this all based on rumour?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you're not right. He went first and foremost to tour the security organs, because for a long time none of us had toured the security organs and that used to be regular practice. To get insight into their work, that was his focus, and also the problems that had to do with violations of international laws of war and to gain his own impressions, that was his first task. The second task was that there were certain objections in view of the engagement of the units of the military police, and he wanted to see that with the commands and to have certain things corrected. That is to say that that was the main reason why he went down there. He did not go to check the work of the MUP or what it was that the MUP was doing and so on and so forth, that was not it at all. However, through briefings, probably, he did get through this information from the chief of the security department and what he had said to him. He probably did not spell out in very concrete terms, because as I said that was not his basic objective. That is what he conveyed to us. We did not deal with the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is it my understanding, then, insofar as you in April were talking about the Skorpions and their one incident; the Arkanovci for which you haven't mentioned any incident; and the Wolves on the Drina for which you did not know what they were doing, your service had no other information about any paramilitaries affiliated with the MUP or any crimes committed by these individuals, apart from that one incident that you keep recycling over and over and over. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, you're not right. You are drawing the wrong conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then please tell me the details. What other paramilitaries, what other crimes, since you said that you have no details? What can you possibly have if you don't have details?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, we had information that was yet again corroborated by Rade Markovic at the meeting of the 17th of May that members of Arkan's group killed a family of Albanians, elderly people. That is what Rade Markovic confirmed at the meeting on the 17th of May, and he said it is correct and he said there is an investigation underway. Those are his words --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it is also correct that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me get very, very basic with you. Are you trying to tell me that you knew about the killing by the reservist JSO, who happened to be a former Arkan member, that Rade Markovic talked about at the May 17th meeting, do you claim that your service knew about that before it happened? Because Rade Markovic said it happened the day before that meeting. Is your service employing clairvoyance?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That question involves elements which I don't think are in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand the question, Mr. Ivetic, in light of the answer from line 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, he said that he had information about this killing, which only occurred the day before the May 17th meeting. So I'm wondering how they could have known about that killing after the Farkas -- at the time of -- prior to the meeting itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I mean, when did you have that information, I guess is the better question to ask you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that that overlapped with the meeting. Before the meeting we had received such information, and then it was confirmed. It just so happened that way, but it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And that -- did your service also confirm the information that Rade Markovic also said at that meeting that the individual who had committed the crime, the killing, this former Arkan who was deployed to Kosovo by Rade Markovic and the JSO, had been processed, he has been arrested by the police and was in the process of being processed for his crime? Did your service have that information?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not have that information. Rade Markovic confirmed this information. He said, Yes, that is correct. And they are under investigation; that is to say that they had been arrested and that they were under investigation. And he used the plural. He said, They are under investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And indeed there were two. I apologise if I misspoke. Now, apart from this crime and the Podujevo crime, your service has no credible verified information of any crimes. I've been asking this several times. Would you please now finally answer because I think we've exhausted all of these references that either you or General Vasiljevic have kept recycling about what Rade Markovic said.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the information we had. We did not have other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- so of the -- of the many problems that General Farkas discussed, only these two could be linked to the so-called MUP paramilitary groups that you guys coined them as, even though your own definition you said they could not be paramilitaries if they were part of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said what I said, and I'm not going to repeat what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now, let's move on. If I can ask you this. Isn't it, in fact, true that one of the reasons for General Farkas's trip was to investigate the information that the service already had about this Pauk group led by Jugoslav Petrusic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Now, you have told us how the service found out about the Pauk group, and you said that you had been following them I think since 1995. I want to put to you the sworn testimony of your colleague and friend General Vasiljevic at transcript page 9008, line 22 through 9009, line 5, wherein he admitted that it was the RDB of the MUP, the State Security Service, that actually first uncovered this Pauk group and rather than reporting it with your service reported it straight to President Milosevic, causing some embarrassment for your service. Do you recall that, sir? If you like, I can quote his exact words if it is necessary, but I'm just trying to jog your memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps counsel should because our computers are crashing and we can't find the exact quote. And I think some aspects like causing embarrassment might be -- might not have been said, as I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, it's the content. Well, let me read the whole quote, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "Q. And when we're talking about Petrusic and Orasanin, am I also -- am I correct that the RDB, the State Security Service, was the initial source of information about Petrusic and his group that ultimately led to the concerns and to the actions that your organs took to arrest these individuals? Answer from General Vasiljevic: "Yes, but the State Security Service did not deliver this information to the military security service; rather, it informed Milosevic of this, and then Milosevic told General Geza about it. This shows what kind of cooperation the MUP had with the army." Now, General Vasiljevic was very angry at the State Security Service for going behind your service's back and going straight to Milosevic with this information. Am I correct that your service felt slighted by these actions of the RDB relating to the uncovery of the Pauk group?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are a few matters here. First of all, when I talked about Jugoslav Petrusic yesterday, I said what I said very precisely. First of all, I said that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... That --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I have to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, you don't. This is a very simple question, absolutely straightforward. Is this right or wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bonomy, it is necessary because what was stated at the outset was something that is incorrect; namely, I did not say that my service in 1995 followed Jugoslav Petrusic. I said that Jugoslav Petrusic from 1995 onwards was re-oriented from the Islamic factor to the Albanian factor, so that is the substantive difference --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, that's immaterial to the question you've been asked at the moment. Please just deal with the question that counsel has asked you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had data about Jugoslav Petrusic from an earlier stage, and we exchanged this information with the State Security Service. So I couldn't -- it wouldn't really be proper to say that they did anything behind our backs, because we had knowledge of who Jugoslav Petrusic was and we exchanged this kind of information with the State Security Service. In light of the view that he was within their operational jurisdiction because he was a civilian, they had to have more information about him and they, in turn, provided this information to whoever needed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did your service need that information and did you receive it from them?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they did not provide information to us on matters that we considered it would have been fair for them to provide information. We did have that problem. I don't know if you had that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, this all occurred before the 17th May meeting with Milosevic, and in fact the concerns over the Pauk group were the -- they were the central theme of that meeting with Milosevic. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was not the central theme. The central theme was the war crimes and other acts that were in contravention with the international law of war and how this should be dealt with together and in a coordinated manner. This was, in fact, a piece of information, an issue, that was dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And knowing that Pauk was going to be an issue that was going to be dealt with, if not the central theme, isn't that the true reason that your service, beginning May 13th, May 16th, leading up to the meeting, all of a sudden wrote all these reports about the Boca Medic group, again recycling that one incident that you had knowledge of on April the 3rd, trying to deflect pressure off of your service over the Pauk debacle. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't agree with you. I think I explained that when I said that on the 13th of May we drafted this report about Skorpions, and we handed it over to the chief of the Supreme Command Staff, and he in turn handed it over to the then-President Milosevic once we were certain about the data that we presented there. I think that was the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I forget if it was after the Farkas trip or after your trip, you indicated that a report that had been created disappeared from the archives. I wanted to ask you: Were there ever any attempts made to reconstruct said report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you probably mean the report that myself and General Vasiljevic drafted after our return from Kosovo on the 7th of June, 1999. We tried to trace this report, even the disks, because everything that was done at the security administration was also copied on to floppy disks, but we were unavailable to do so. Myself and General Vasiljevic tried to reconstruct that in some way, but during the NATO air-strikes, substantial portions of the security administration archives were destroyed. It is possible that it was there and that it also got destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you said that you knew -- let's get to this 17th May meeting and I'd like to discuss the RDB personnel who were former Arkan's people. You claim that you knew about these Arkan individuals that were in the JSO in Kosovo. What were your sources for this information?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I can't recall, and this is about the third time counsel has said it, where the witness said anything about these -- him knowing them to be in the JSO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You said that you knew these men were in Kosovo. What were -- what were your sources?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were our operational sources that we had among them and various sources, operational sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you name names, positions? I'm not really satisfied with just the generic sources. Okay.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I can't give you their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you understand Markovic as saying that he had deployed these people into Legija's unit?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say you had knowledge of the fact that two of these individuals had been involved in the crime of an elderly Albanian couple, did your information correlate with the information --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Um -- I don't want to keep jumping up, but again I think the witness said they were involved, that Markovic told him they, and he stressed the plural; and counsel said two.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I guess I'm going to the evidence that we have already in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: They, the information that they had committed a crime, did that -- did that coincide with the information that Markovic gave to you at the meeting, that one crime?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did Markovic mention the locale where that crime had occurred?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I would like to move along to the Wolves on the Drina which you keep bringing up, but for this which you don't give us much information. Now, you stated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I think I remember them being mentioned once, and perhaps I asked a question; but beyond that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: He raised them to me as well today, Your Honour, twice, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I've missed those.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: They weren't even questions to them. I just asked generally and he kept repeating Arkan's men, these men from Republika Srpska, which are the Wolves from the Drina, he might not have used the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I see, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me get to this. He did say they were mentioned with the man Legenda, who he say was Karasek. Let's try and get this cleared up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, on the 7th of September, that is, the other day, for that day it was transcript page 108, line 16, you stated that among the topics at the 17th May meeting with Milosevic were the so-called paramilitary group from the Republika Srpska Wolves of the Drina. Can you remember specifically what was said about them?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This group was mentioned in the context of Arkan, and Medic, a.k.a. Boca, and in his introductory remarks General Vasiljevic mentioned them, but there was no further discussion on them. Specifically, the Drina Wolves were not mentioned again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'd like to explore some of the information that your service has from following this group. First of all, to make sure that we're talking about the right group. Am I correct that the Wolves of the Drina were essentially an armed group that operated in Republika Srpska -- actually, they were a formal member of the Zvornik Brigade in the Army of the Republika Srpska, with an emblem of a wolf on their shoulder and a captain leading them, captain first class, whose nickname was Legenda. Is that the same group that we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to say that you provided more details than I was aware of, but as I already said, this was a group, its name was the Drina Wolves, and their boss was Nedeljko Karasek, a.k.a., Legenda, before the war he was the commander of the special anti-terrorist units in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You said that. I'm just trying to see how good your information is with your service, sir. Now what was the source of this information and did you consider that information to be verified and credible?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We considered this information to be reliable and authenticated because some sources had been from the Republika Srpska area and they knew Nedeljko Karasek and those people who were trained there, and we also had sources on our side so to speak. So the sources here were quite reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I see. Quite reliable. Are you familiar with captain first class Milan Jolovic and his role commanding the Wolves of the Drina in the Republika Srpska under the nickname Legenda?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your sources didn't know about his connection to this group, did they?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, as far as I can recall, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did your sources or your information indicate that Captain First Class Jolovic, a.k.a. Legenda, left the army of the Serb republic and joined the Army of Yugoslavia after the Dayton Accords?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know a man by the name of Jolovic. I don't know if his nickname was Legenda, who was in Republika Srpska, in the Republika Srpska army. I think he was also in the 10th Sabotage Detachment, if that's the one. Indeed, later on he went on to join the Army of Yugoslavia, but he did not remain in its rank for long, he was demobilised, if that's the Jolovic that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The Jolovic I'm talking about, last rank of colonel, just retired from the VJ a couple months ago, Milan Jolovic, a.k.a. Legenda, who served in Kosovo with the 72nd Special Brigade of the VJ. Is it possible that your sources mixed up their information, considering they didn't know that Legenda was Jolovic and not Karasek?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, because let me give you another example. We had Milorad Ulemek nicknamed Legija --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What do Ulemek have to do with the Wolves of the Drina. I'm trying to focus on group by group to find out exactly what you knew and why every time I ask a difficult question you jump to Arkan, I don't know. But I'd like to ask you is it possible that your information was incorrect, given that they didn't know that the commander Legenda, of the Wolves of the Drina, was this professional soldier Milan Jolovic and not Nedeljko Karaska?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am ruling out this possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Does your service know if Legenda, Jolovic, was in Kosovo with the 72nd Special Brigade? I presume he had a security officer in that detachment.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had it, but I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Are you aware of the fact that after leaving the Republika Srpska SAJ, which is a different SAJ than the one that's under the MUP of Serbia, Mr. Karasek held several positions within the government of the Republika Srpska entity in Bosnia, including deputy minister of the interior; but that in 1997 he moved on and after that date had no affiliation with the MUP of either Republika Srpska or the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he did various things. I don't know about his further activities because we did not follow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Mr. Karasek relocated to Belgrade, where he resided during the entire duration of the NATO onslaught, air war?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to move on to Kosovo Polje. You said that all these groups were based in Kosovo Polje. Do you happen to know how large, geographically speaking, or population-wise Kosovo Polje is?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, what you say is not correct. I didn't say that all those groups were based in Kosovo Polje. I said that there was a centre in Kosovo Polje and that is linked with Arkan, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's focus on the centre in Kosovo Polje because we had a witness come here, Mr. Odalovic, who was from Kosovo Polje who was in Kosovo Polje during the time period of the war, and he testified that the official SAJ base was located near his house in Kosovo Polje. Did you have information about the fact that the official SAJ base was in Kosovo Polje during the war, and is that perhaps this nebulous centre that your rumours and security organs keep going on and on about?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that the base was there. This is the information that we had, to the effect that Arkan was in that centre, and that's what we presented --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir: Given the training that you know your security organs receive, don't you find it rather implausible that the same security organ who is observing Kosovo Polje knows of a centre for Arkan but does not know of an official SAJ base? How could he miss something like that, sir?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't quite put the spin on it. He probably knew that, but if this was a legal base, a legitimate base, that's not something that he was dealing with. He was not dealing with a legitimate MUP base or anything. What he was interested in was what was really important. So he probably knew about the base and he probably visited the base, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So you go from not knowing -- having any information about it to speculating how he perhaps visited the base. Is that how your service worked, sir? Is it true that it's a lot of guesswork and speculation? Because that's the impression that I'm getting.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think you're going about this in an improper way, and I really don't like the way you are questioning me. I think that some rules and -- have to be respected and the dignity has to be respected. You're asking tendentious questions that have nothing to do with anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wouldn't like to get involved before this, but I think that the witness was asked whether he had information, and he gave us this answer. And then he was asked about the security organ or his service, he was asked to tell us about that. I think that the witness was quite clear in giving his answer to the initial question, and now as to how the witness dealt with the second question, I leave it up to Mr. Ivetic to decide whether it was what he wanted or not; but I think that this impropriety is something that is there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I consider the question to be perfectly properly framed. The witness has twice said that his source probably knew. He could tell us an answer to the most recent question how he comes to that conclusion if it's not speculation. Mr. Gajic, we don't think that anything improper has taken place here. If you want to explain how it is you can say that your source probably knew about the base, then tell us; but unless you can give a basis, then it may well be no more than speculation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Security organs report on things that are very -- that have a very narrow counter-intelligence focus. Some things that are matter of course, that are not something that his superiors would be interested in, that have nothing to do with counter-intelligence, for instance, that he was sitting in a house with a friend of his, this is not something that he would report, this is not something that we would be interested in. So I said that it is possible that this security organ went to this base, that he was aware of that base, but that was not something that he reported because he thought that it was not essential at all. We did not monitor the MUP or its activities; we did not have the jurisdiction to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. You are entitled to say: I don't know, when you are asked a question that you don't know the answer to. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have about ten more questions but I see we're at the quarter past -- quarter till mark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We can have our break at this stage. We have to break again for 20 minutes.. Mr. Gajic, please go with the usher. And we'll resume at five minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We're very grateful to you, Mr. Stamp, for dealing with these two matters raised at the beginning so quickly, and we can now grant both the fourth request that was made by Mr. Ojdanic and Mr. Sainovic's application to correct the identification of the passages in the video. We'll sit in this session until 5.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General Gajic, in dealing with these groups that you said were in Kosovo Polje, and you indicated they all wore SAJ uniforms. I don't suppose you have any information as to the specific details of those uniforms, the insignia thereupon, and their locations; if so, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. We don't have that. We didn't particularly investigate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, one thing you did say you particularly investigated and that you followed in detail was the movements of this group of Boca Medic, and you indicated you knew of their redeployment back into Kosovo and Metohija. Did your information include where they were deployed and based during that second deployment to Kosovo-Metohija?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I recall, I think it was in the broader area of Kosovo, but I don't know if it was Kosovo Polje or something else. I really couldn't specifically say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, Mr. Stoparic again, the Prosecution witness who is an SAJ reservist and a former Skorpion testified on the 13th of July, transcript page 783 to 784 line 4 that when his group was redeployed to Kosovo, that is to say his reserve unit of the SAJ that included some former Skorpions, they were beginning the 15th or 16th of April onwards deployed in Kosovo Polje. Now, I want to ask you insofar as your information is very clear about the Arkan's men wearing SAJ uniforms in Kosovo Polje, how is it possible that you aren't sure whether the SAJ reservists wearing SAJ uniforms that are former Skorpions were in Kosovo Polje? How can that be and is it possible that your operative is mixing again these individuals with the individuals that he says are Arkan's people?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he's not mixing them up. We even felt that after they came back, after the incident in Podujevo, that they would not be brought back to Kosovo, and they did appear. So our operative registered that through his sources and reported that; namely, that they came back again and that the agreement that they would no longer appear was not respected.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Is it the same source, talking about following the Skorpions and reporting their movements, as is for Arkan's people, is it the same person, the same individual?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were different sources, not just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you then concede the possibility that the one source following the Skorpions knows the Skorpions are in Kosovo Polje, but the other source, not knowing who the Skorpions are, sees some people he has knowledge of from their participation in other wars and assumes them to be Arkan's people? Do you concede that is a possibility, given that two separate sources covering the same locale report about two separate groups, but neither one of them reports about both groups being in that locale?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I rule out that possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Based upon what, sir, what verified, credible, uncontrovertible evidence do you have to exclude that possibility in your own mind?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because Boca Medic and Arkan- and I said that they appeared for a long time in the roles that they appeared in, and our operatives in Kosovo and outside Kosovo knew them both by appearance, Arkan, Medic, and a majority of their members. I said we had sources among them that we talked with and who provided information to us. So the possibility that there was some kind of mix-up or substitution is ruled out.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I see. Now you're changing the story to say that Arkan himself was in Kosovo Polje; is that it? Because that's not what's been said to date. To date it's been said that certain individuals, 30 individuals from Arkan's group of 100 were offered were deployed by Ratko Markovic, the RDB chief in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that Arkan was there. I said that our operatives in Kosovo and outside Kosovo knew Arkan and Medic, they knew them by appearance. I never said that Arkan was in Kosovo, however, Arkan personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, last question about these groups. The Wolves of the Drina, based upon your information, as vast as it is, where were they based or deploy and during what time-period?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was also in the Kosovo Polje area, and we had information even that they were in private houses. This was the time when Medic, Boca Medic, was there, too, perhaps a little bit earlier or a little bit later, but it's more or less that time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, I have just one more thing related to your testimony yesterday that I was a little baffled on. Are you genuinely telling us that you are not sure who Colonel Milorad Stupar is and where he was during the Kosovo war? Because I have information that he was with you in the high command of the VJ during most of that time-period. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't confirm that. The only thing that I know, because that was also an issue, is that on the 14th of April when the order was drafted on the acceptance of volunteers --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stupar wasn't there, but, yes, I know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you know what role he held during the NATO bombing?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that for a while he worked in the infantry administration, since he is an infantry man, but perhaps he was in some other duties, too. But I think that for a while he was at the infantry administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour, I think I have maybe one more question for this witness. I just want to check something.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm completed with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gajic, for your time and cooperation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. You'll now be examined by the Prosecutor, Mr. Stamp. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can I start -- well, good afternoon, General. Can I start by just briefly taking up --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Taking up where we left off in respect to the paramilitaries. You said that the Drina Wolves, the Skorpions, the Arkan's men, they wore SAJ uniforms, although you could not describe any particular insignia on those uniforms, you mean the normal, regular, SAJ uniforms they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know that it is an offence to impersonate the police -- or it was an offence to impersonate the police in 1999 in Serbia --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object to this question in so far as the evidence that I led established that they were all members of the police, so I don't think this question has any basis or foundation in the cross-examination that was conducted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I can't see why, having regard to what counsel is saying, that is question is impermissible, but I could move on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I agree with you. The witness has given more than one definition of a paramilitary. So there is no reason why you cannot ask this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, was it illegal to impersonate the police?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I understand. You are saying that persons who were not members of the police could pretend or wear police uniforms legally?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is illegal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I take you back just a little. You were asked at the beginning there if these various groups wore regular SAJ uniforms, and your answer was rather ambiguous. You said: "You could say that, yes." Now, what was the position? Were they or were they not wearing regular SAJ uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the special units of the police, there is the special anti-terrorist unit, "Specijalne Antiteroristcke Jedinice," and the other units that I know of, the "Posebne Jedinice Policije," are special units that are used for some specific assignments but can be used for some anti-terrorist activities. So I think a more correct answer would be that they wore insignia of the police, that they didn't have insignia. Some of them perhaps had SAJ insignia, but for the most part they wore police insignia. I think that that would be a more proper and more correct reply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm trying to look at your answer here. Well, let me just ask you the question directly. When you say they wore -- they wore -- for the most part they wore police insignia, you mean regular police attached to the RJB, that is, public security of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If we are talking about the groups that we mentioned before, these are not regular police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- They did not go through the procedure, because the Law on Defence has Article 18, regulating how the ranks of the military and the ranks of the MUP are replenished. In paragraph 2 of that law it is said that --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Thanks. I --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I just wanted to complete the sentence. I apologise to the Prosecutor. Paragraph 2 of that Article 18 it says that organs and units of MUP are replenished with military conscripts; in order to have the forces replenished with military conscripts, it has to go through the military districts as the military territorial organs. If the military districts are not used and they are bypassed, this means that the law is being violated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. Your earlier answer I think you referred to special units of the police and you went on to say that for the most part these units that we are speaking about wore police insignia.
